## 6. Trust boundaries

- Environment variables and workspace YAML are the untrusted admission channels. Controls: strict field allowlist, type parsing, bounded ranges, enum validation, fail-closed errors (§2.3).
- Values admitted as free-form strings that flow onward without enumeration at this layer: `agentwrap.sandbox` and `agentwrap.permission_mode` (cast into agentwrap enums at request build time, runtime/runtime.go:598-611; whether agentwrap validates them downstream is external to this repo — see Unknowns); `agentwrap.env` entries (`KEY=value` forwarded to runtime processes via `WithEnv`, opencode.go:39, and `cmd.Env` appends at opencode.go:108,182); planning model identifiers (become provider/model IDs).
- Redaction boundary: applied before stdout in `config show` (whole projection) and per-field in `health` (messages/guidance). Marker-based detection (substring heuristics, §2.4), not a secret-type system. `Sources`, counts (`environment.overrides`), durations, limits render unredacted by design (documented as safe: docs/configuration.md:235-250).
- Health forwards provider/model/workdir/check IDs to the agentwrap library and executes the configured `agentwrap.executable`; the workspace path is user-selected via flag/env/cwd walk-up.

## 7. External effects

- Subprocess execution only in the health runtime phase: agentwrap `CheckHealth`/`Capabilities` against the configured OpenCode executable (indirect via library; UltraPlan-side entry `NewOpenCode` opencode.go:31-127 also constructs a rate-table store under `os.UserCacheDir()/ultraplan`).
- Stdout/stderr writes. No filesystem writes, no network calls owned by this layer (provider access happens inside agentwrap during live health checks such as authentication/provider probes).

## 8. Cancellation / retry / restart / error semantics

- Context: `deps.ctx` derives from SIGINT/SIGTERM notify-context in main; consumed by `adapter.Health` (CheckHealth/Capabilities). Config loading, validation, redaction, rendering are synchronous and not context-aware.
- Retry: none inside this surface; retry/backoff policy belongs to the runtime stack (`NewOpenCode` composes `BasicPolicy{MaxAttemptsPerTarget: DefaultRetries+1, ...}`, opencode.go:52-56) and is out of scope here.
- Restart/recovery: not applicable (stateless); re-running re-reads inputs.
- Errors: fail-closed classification — bad args ExitUsage(2); discovery ExitWorkspace(4); load/validate ExitConfig(3); runtime health failure ExitRuntime(6); structure invalid ExitValidation(5); write failures on stdout fall back to ExitError(1)/ExitOK handling in `fail`/`writeStatus` (app.go:229-248). `health` deliberately continues collecting checks under partial failure (degraded report + classified exit). `config show`/`loadEffectiveConfig` abort at first error.

## 1. Purpose

Layered configuration resolution for the UltraPlan CLI. Effective configuration is computed per process invocation from four layers — built-in defaults → workspace `ultraplan.yml` → `ULTRAPLAN_*` environment variables → CLI overrides — with typed parsing, bounded validation, per-field provenance (`Sources`), and marker-based secret redaction before any human-visible output. Three operator commands expose this surface: `config show [--json]`, `health [--json]`, and `version`. The same effective config feeds every other surface (sprint, study, run, serve, tui), including sandbox/permission grants passed into the agentwrap runtime stack. No durable state is written by this surface; it is read-only over workspace files plus environment admission.

## 6. Trust boundaries

- Environment variables and workspace YAML are the untrusted admission channels. Controls: strict field allowlist, type parsing, bounded ranges, enum validation, fail-closed errors (§2.3).
- Values admitted as free-form strings that flow onward without enumeration at this layer: `agentwrap.sandbox` and `agentwrap.permission_mode` (cast into agentwrap enums at request build time, runtime/runtime.go:598-611; whether agentwrap validates them downstream is external to this repo — see Unknowns); `agentwrap.env` entries (`KEY=value` forwarded to runtime processes via `WithEnv`, opencode.go:39, and `cmd.Env` appends at opencode.go:108,182); planning model identifiers (become provider/model IDs).
- Redaction boundary: applied before stdout in `config show` (whole projection) and per-field in `health` (messages/guidance). Marker-based detection (substring heuristics, §2.4), not a secret-type system. `Sources`, counts (`environment.overrides`), durations, limits render unredacted by design (documented as safe: docs/configuration.md:235-250).
- Health forwards provider/model/workdir/check IDs to the agentwrap library and executes the configured `agentwrap.executable`; the workspace path is user-selected via flag/env/cwd walk-up.

## 7. External effects

- Subprocess execution only in the health runtime phase: agentwrap `CheckHealth`/`Capabilities` against the configured OpenCode executable (indirect via library; UltraPlan-side entry `NewOpenCode` opencode.go:31-127 also constructs a rate-table store under `os.UserCacheDir()/ultraplan`).
- Stdout/stderr writes. No filesystem writes, no network calls owned by this layer (provider access happens inside agentwrap during live health checks such as authentication/provider probes).

## 8. Cancellation / retry / restart / error semantics

- Context: `deps.ctx` derives from SIGINT/SIGTERM notify-context in main; consumed by `adapter.Health` (CheckHealth/Capabilities). Config loading, validation, redaction, rendering are synchronous and not context-aware.
- Retry: none inside this surface; retry/backoff policy belongs to the runtime stack (`NewOpenCode` composes `BasicPolicy{MaxAttemptsPerTarget: DefaultRetries+1, ...}`, opencode.go:52-56) and is out of scope here.
- Restart/recovery: not applicable (stateless); re-running re-reads inputs.
- Errors: fail-closed classification — bad args ExitUsage(2); discovery ExitWorkspace(4); load/validate ExitConfig(3); runtime health failure ExitRuntime(6); structure invalid ExitValidation(5); write failures on stdout fall back to ExitError(1)/ExitOK handling in `fail`/`writeStatus` (app.go:229-248). `health` deliberately continues collecting checks under partial failure (degraded report + classified exit). `config show`/`loadEffectiveConfig` abort at first error.

## 1. Purpose

Layered configuration resolution for the UltraPlan CLI. Effective configuration is computed per process invocation from four layers — built-in defaults → workspace `ultraplan.yml` → `ULTRAPLAN_*` environment variables → CLI overrides — with typed parsing, bounded validation, per-field provenance (`Sources`), and marker-based secret redaction before any human-visible output. Three operator commands expose this surface: `config show [--json]`, `health [--json]`, and `version`. The same effective config feeds every other surface (sprint, study, run, serve, tui), including sandbox/permission grants passed into the agentwrap runtime stack. No durable state is written by this surface; it is read-only over workspace files plus environment admission.

## 2. Entrypoints and control flow

### 2.1 Dispatch (REALITY)

`cmd/ultraplan/main.go:18-43` builds `app.Config` (signal context from `signal.NotifyContext(SIGINT, SIGTERM)`, `Version: app.DefaultVersion()`) and calls `app.Run`.

`internal/app/app.go:88-178` (`Run`):

### 2.3 Config load pipeline (internal/platform/config/config.go)

`Load` (config.go:153-179):
1. start from `Defaults()` (config.go:181-195); pre-seed `Sources[field]="default"` for all 53 scalar fields + 28 QA fields;
2. parse `<root>/ultraplan.yml` via hand-rolled line parser `loadFile` (config.go:197-269);
3. apply env overrides `applyEnv` (config.go:275-288) over `EnvOverrides()` = 27 explicit keys (config.go:120-151) + 28 generated `ULTRAPLAN_QA_*` keys (qa.go:94-105); only non-empty values are applied; parse errors wrap the env key name and do not claim source (config_test.go:326-339);
4. apply CLI overrides — only `Logging.Format`/`Logging.Level` pointers exist (`CLIOverrides.LogFormat/LogLevel`, config.go:103-107); source "cli";
5. `Validate(e.Config)` (config.go:175-177).

YAML parser facts (config.go:197-269): blank/`#`-comment lines skipped; unindented `key:` starts a section; indented `key:` that names one of 5 list fields (`agentwrap.required_health|required_capabilities|extra_args|env`, `smoke.environment`) clears the list and activates list mode; `- item` appends (double-quote trimming); otherwise `key: value` scalars via first-colon split, double quotes trimmed; unknown field ⇒ `unknown config field %q` (config.go:420); a line without a colon ⇒ `unsupported line`. Trailing inline comments are not stripped. Not a general YAML implementation (no flow lists, anchors, multi-line scalars).

`setField` (config.go:290-423) maps dotted field paths to typed setters; ints via `strconv.Atoi`, quota via `ParseInt`; QA fields delegated to `setQAField` (qa.go:107-183).

`Validate` (config.go:425-538) enforced bounds:
- `version == 1`; required non-empty: `runtime.default`, `models.default/primary/backup`, `execution.default_variant`, `agentwrap.executable`; `runtime.default == "opencode"`;
- `execution.default_parallel > 0`, `default_retries >= 0`, `default_timeout` positive duration;
- smoke: discovery ≤ 5m, run ≤ 24h, cleanup_grace ≤ 30s (all positive); stdout_limit ∈ [1, 64 MiB]; stderr_limit ∈ [1, 16 MiB]; env names must match `^[A-Z_][A-Z0-9_]*$` (validEnvName, config.go:577-587);
- git: stage_completion ∈ {off, commit, commit-and-push}; remote charset `[A-Za-z0-9._/-]`, no leading `-`; push_timeout ∈ (0, 30m];
- run_control: full_history ≥ 1h; tombstone_history ≥ 24h and ≥ full_history; quota ≥ 64 MiB;

None durable. Effective config is recomputed per invocation. Inputs read: `ultraplan.yml` at the discovered root, directory structure, environment. The scaffolded `ultraplan.yml` content is embedded at `internal/workspace/init.go:137-175` (`const defaultConfig`) — note the scaffold does not include `git:`/`run_control:` sections even though docs/configuration.md:73-76 shows them in the "Default ultraplan.yml" listing (another doc/source divergence fact; defaults still apply at load time). `Sources` provenance lives only in memory within `config.Effective`.

## 5. Invariants (as implemented and/or documented)

REALITY (code/tests):
- I1 Precedence order defaults < workspace < env < CLI is enforced by sequential overwrite in `Load`; provenance records last writer ("default"/"workspace"/"env"/"cli").
- I2 Unknown YAML/env field names are rejected at load (fail-closed admission).
- I3 All documented bounds in §2.3 hold after both YAML and env application (single `Validate` post-merge).
- I4 Malformed env integers/durations abort load with the env key named; source stays "default".
- I5 Every value rendered by `config show` passes through `Redact`; every health message/guidance passes through `RedactValue` (twice: at construction and again in `sanitizeHealthChecks`).
- I6 Health never executes runtime checks unless config validation succeeded.
- I7 Runtime-required health checks and capabilities accepted at admission are exactly the sets known to the runtime mapper (`knownHealth`/`knownCapability` mirror `mapHealthIDs`/`mapCapabilitiesIDs`), so config-driven mapping cannot produce "unsupported id" errors.
- I8 `health` exit-code precedence: config > runtime > structure.

CURRENT-CONTRACT (planning workspace):
- C1 Configuration contract (system/contracts/core/configuration.md): CFG-SOURCE-001 explicit sources/precedence; CFG-TYPE-001 typed+validated; CFG-SECRET-001 secrets separated/redacted (Blocker); CFG-START-001 fail before work starts (Blocker); CFG-OBS-001 effective non-secret config inspectable; CFG-PUBLIC-001 allowlisted public config.
- C2 CLI contract (system/contracts/surfaces/cli.md): CLI-CONFIG-001 documented inspectable precedence, "redact secrets in config display" (cli.md:153); CLI-EXIT-001 stable exit codes; CLI-JSON-001 stable machine-readable output; CLI-HELP-001 help/version.
- C3 Sprint 02 requirements (projects/ultraplan-go/sprints/02-workspace-config-health/requirements.md:47-53): precedence chain, redaction, deterministic text+JSON, meaningful exit codes.
- C4 Product docs (docs/configuration.md): validation rejection list (§Validation), runtime/model mapping table (§Runtime And Model Mapping incl. sandbox/permission mapping, line 216), redaction policy ("Do not place provider tokens in ultraplan.yml", §Redaction), run-control bounds table.

FUTURE-INTENT (not current defect basis): release-checklist version-metadata expectations; web policy note that adding configurable overrides requires named fields/ranges/source reporting/fail-closed tests (docs/configuration.md:162-180).

## 6. Trust boundaries

- Environment variables and workspace YAML are the untrusted admission channels. Controls: strict field allowlist, type parsing, bounded ranges, enum validation, fail-closed errors (§2.3).
- Values admitted as free-form strings that flow onward without enumeration at this layer: `agentwrap.sandbox` and `agentwrap.permission_mode` (cast into agentwrap enums at request build time, runtime/runtime.go:598-611; whether agentwrap validates them downstream is external to this repo — see Unknowns); `agentwrap.env` entries (`KEY=value` forwarded to runtime processes via `WithEnv`, opencode.go:39, and `cmd.Env` appends at opencode.go:108,182); planning model identifiers (become provider/model IDs).
- Redaction boundary: applied before stdout in `config show` (whole projection) and per-field in `health` (messages/guidance). Marker-based detection (substring heuristics, §2.4), not a secret-type system. `Sources`, counts (`environment.overrides`), durations, limits render unredacted by design (documented as safe: docs/configuration.md:235-250).
- Health forwards provider/model/workdir/check IDs to the agentwrap library and executes the configured `agentwrap.executable`; the workspace path is user-selected via flag/env/cwd walk-up.

## 7. External effects

- Subprocess execution only in the health runtime phase: agentwrap `CheckHealth`/`Capabilities` against the configured OpenCode executable (indirect via library; UltraPlan-side entry `NewOpenCode` opencode.go:31-127 also constructs a rate-table store under `os.UserCacheDir()/ultraplan`).
- Stdout/stderr writes. No filesystem writes, no network calls owned by this layer (provider access happens inside agentwrap during live health checks such as authentication/provider probes).

## 8. Cancellation / retry / restart / error semantics

- Context: `deps.ctx` derives from SIGINT/SIGTERM notify-context in main; consumed by `adapter.Health` (CheckHealth/Capabilities). Config loading, validation, redaction, rendering are synchronous and not context-aware.
- Retry: none inside this surface; retry/backoff policy belongs to the runtime stack (`NewOpenCode` composes `BasicPolicy{MaxAttemptsPerTarget: DefaultRetries+1, ...}`, opencode.go:52-56) and is out of scope here.
- Restart/recovery: not applicable (stateless); re-running re-reads inputs.
- Errors: fail-closed classification — bad args ExitUsage(2); discovery ExitWorkspace(4); load/validate ExitConfig(3); runtime health failure ExitRuntime(6); structure invalid ExitValidation(5); write failures on stdout fall back to ExitError(1)/ExitOK handling in `fail`/`writeStatus` (app.go:229-248). `health` deliberately continues collecting checks under partial failure (degraded report + classified exit). `config show`/`loadEffectiveConfig` abort at first error.

## 9. Files, symbols, tests, contracts

Primary production files:
- internal/platform/config/config.go — Config/Effective/LoadOptions/CLIOverrides, EnvOverrides, Load, Defaults, loadFile, applyEnv, setField, Validate, helpers (validGitRemoteName, validEnvName, knownHealth, knownCapability, list handling).
- internal/platform/config/qa.go — QA struct, DefaultQA/maxQA, qaConfigFields/QAConfigFields, qaEnvOverrides, setQAField/setQAInteger, validateQA. Doc comment states the lower-only doctrine (qa.go:10-12).
- internal/platform/config/redaction.go — redacted marker, Redacted projection, Sensitive/RedactValue/redactModels/redactPlanning/redactAgentwrap.
- internal/platform/config/doc.go — package doc noting deferred-sprint framing.
- internal/platform/runtime/health.go — HealthRequest/HealthReport/Capabilities types, Adapter.Health, mapCapabilities, healthStatus.
- internal/platform/runtime/agentwrap.go — mapHealthIDs/mapCapabilitiesIDs/mapPermissionPolicy (+payload sanitization helpers used elsewhere).
- internal/platform/runtime/opencode.go — NewOpenCode (executable/args/env/stderr limit mapping; retry policy; backup fallback), requestVariantRuntime.
- internal/platform/runtime/runtime.go:22-78,526-614 — Request/PermissionPolicy structs, Adapter.Capabilities, RequestFromConfig, toAgentwrapRequest (enum casts, policy validation via agentwrap.ValidatePermissionPolicy).
- internal/app/app.go — dispatch, exit codes, discoverWorkspace/envLookup/loadEffectiveConfig (287-319), renderVersion.
- internal/app/config_commands.go — runConfig, configHelp/configShowHelp.
- internal/app/health_commands.go — runHealth, runRuntimeHealth, runtimeGuidance, sanitizeHealthChecks, envSummary, healthHelp, seam var runtimeHealthChecks.
- internal/app/version.go — Version/DefaultVersion/IsZero.
- internal/app/json_output.go — writeJSON envelope (jsonEnvelopeSchemaVersion=1, timeNow seam).
- Dependency surface (read-only consumers of this pack): internal/workspace/discovery.go, validation.go, init.go (scaffold const defaultConfig at init.go:137-175).

Tests (REALITY):
- internal/platform/config/config_test.go — precedence+validation (TestLoadPrecedenceAndValidation), redaction incl. dash-form api key (TestRedactSensitiveValues:79-100), list-then-scalar agentwrap ordering (TestLoadAgentwrapListThenScalarFields), bad timeout/smoke env-name/git/run-control/runtime-mapping rejections, QA count=28/sources/lower-only matrix, malformed-QA-env source discipline, unknown-QA-field error ordering, QA workspace<env precedence.
- internal/app/app_test.go — TestRunHelp, TestRunVersion (injected metadata), TestConfigShowJSONRedactsAndUsesWorkspace (envelope fields, sources map, code_context values from scaffold), TestConfigShowTextIncludesRequiredHealth; shared harness initializedWorkspace/runForTest*.

- Note (naming divergence, neutral): sprint-02 requirements list `config_commands_test.go`, `redaction_test.go`, `output.go`, `logging` skeleton outputs (requirements.md:27-40); actual tree consolidates these tests into config_test.go/app_test.go, output helpers live in json_output.go, internal/platform/logging exists separately. Coverage intent persists despite file moves.

Contracts (CURRENT-CONTRACT): configuration contract, CLI contract, sprint-02 requirements/handbook, target docs/configuration.md + docs/cli-reference.md + docs/architecture.md (as product documentation). Baseline: go test ./..., -race, vet all pass at frozen commit (review/state.json).

Downstream consumption map (who eats `config.Effective`):
- run_commands.go:50,255; study_commands.go:319,676,861; tui_commands.go:33; serve_commands.go:41; sprint_commands.go:84,686 — all via loadEffectiveConfig.
- sprint service assembly: qaSettings (sprint_commands.go:713-787; fallback chain qa.model → planning.review_model → planning.plan_model → models.default; variant → execution.default_variant; duration re-parse; sprint.ValidateQASettings re-check), smokeSettings (814-823; duration re-parse ignoring errors because load already validated; Getenv seam), planningStageRuntime (894+), review concurrency = Execution.DefaultParallel, publisher = stagePublisher(Config.Git...).
- Runtime stack: RequestFromConfig (runtime.go:537-560: primary/default split, timeout, RequireHealth/Caps, Sandbox, Permissions, PermissionPolicy{Default, UnsupportedBehavior}); NewOpenCode (executable, extra_args, env, stderr limit, retries+1 attempts, backup fallback when ≠primary); toAgentwrapRequest casts Sandbox/Permissions to agentwrap enum types and validates PermissionPolicy (agentwrap.go:75-101).

## 10. Immediate surface dependencies

- **workspace-scaffold-defaults** (declared): provides marker-file semantics, `Validate` required structure, embedded scaffold `ultraplan.yml` content that seeds typical values seen by `config show`.
- Consumed-by (downstream surfaces receiving effective config): sprint-flow-state/planning-chain/execute-resume/conformance-review/qa-investigation/smoke-gate, study surfaces, run-cli-observation, serve/tui, opencode-agent-runtime (sandbox/permission grants), repo-publication (git settings), run-control (retention/quota).

## 11. Explicit unknowns

1. Whether agentwrap (github.com/Antonio7098/agentwrap v0.0.0-20260825130518-dccd575bd101) validates `SandboxMode`/`PermissionMode` string values at request/run time, and what CheckHealth actually executes — external dependency internals were not inspected here.
2. How release builds are intended to stamp `version` metadata (no ldflags wiring found in-tree; release-checklist wording is intent-level).
3. Behavior class of the hand-rolled YAML subset vs. real-world YAML users might write (e.g., tabs, flow lists, nested deeper than one level, duplicate keys) beyond what the parser visibly accepts/rejects; duplicate scalar keys silently last-write-win per the loop structure.
4. Whether any deployment populates `CLIOverrides.LogFormat/LogLevel` outside unit tests (none found in-tree today).
5. Live behavior of `environment.overrides` counting under set-but-empty vars (counted only when non-empty, matching applyEnv) — consistent by inspection, no dedicated test for empty-string case.
6. Interaction between `ULTRAPLAN_CODE_CONTEXT_MODEL/_VARIANT` being absent from docs/configuration.md's env list and operator expectations (documentation completeness question, flagged as fact in §3, not judged).
